context.objective: Document how we carry out Monitoring Fee Billing & Revenue Recognition, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: For One Rock we review the monitoring-fee schedule about 30 days before quarter end. The fund team confirms investments, exits and fee changes. We draft invoices in Sage, obtain internal review and client approval, then send them typically around the 15th before quarter end. The first business day of the quarter is when approved invoices are posted.
How are the monitoring-fee amounts on the schedule calculated and updated when investments, exits or fee changes occur?

We use the current schedule and the management agreement, check the fee for each portfolio company and associated fund, and update for changes confirmed by the One Rock fund team. A company lacking agreement support is flagged. I cannot give one formula for every company's base fee. The subsequent offset accrual is separate: it uses fee activity, ownership and LP percentages and fund factors from current workpapers. The approved version and sign convention for the offset still need confirmation.
What does the internal review compare the drafted invoices against before they go to the client?

The preparer and an internal reviewer compare the unposted Sage drafts with the current schedule and approved support: portfolio company, address or contact, fund, fee, period and reference. We resolve review comments, obtain One Rock fund team or client approval, then retain approval and proof of sending. Posting is later. Normal posting is Dr 1100 / Cr 4005, and the full amount is recognized on the invoice date.
What happens to a portfolio company flagged for lacking agreement support before its invoice is sent?

The preparer flags missing agreement support and confirms the change with the One Rock fund team. The documented route requires the support to be resolved and client approval before sending. We separately track manual or outside-Sage invoicing and a client instruction to hold. If a manual invoice is needed, we wait for an approved manual procedure. I cannot supply an approved manual procedure.
When One Rock instructs you to hold an invoice, what happens to it before it can be sent or posted?

If One Rock says to hold before issue, we retain the written instruction and status, and delay the invoice until told to continue. If the direction is to issue now but delay revenue, the approved treatment is an open policy question. Those are different cases. We can't decide to defer the revenue on our own.
What practical effect, if any, does an invoice hold or unresolved revenue-treatment instruction have on billing or quarter-end close?

The held item stays open on the schedule and the invoice is delayed until One Rock instructs release. For an instruction to bill but delay recognition, the affected posting stays open pending an approved policy. Late or unsupported posting would make the quarter's revenue and monitoring fee offset unreliable; the team compares 4005 activity and the offset accrual to workpapers at close.
After posting, what do you compare at close, and what tells you the billing and revenue work is complete?

summary: For One Rock, the team reviews the monitoring-fee schedule, drafts and reviews invoices, obtains approval and sends them before later posting. Held invoices remain open until release; postings affected by a bill-now, recognize-later instruction await an approved policy. At close, the team compares revenue activity and the separate offset accrual to workpapers.
parking_lot: Confirm the approved version and sign convention for the separate offset accrual.
Confirm the approved treatment when an invoice is issued now but revenue is delayed.
